body:
I can confirm the problem exists even in `v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]` (Windows 10) using `WebSocketMultiplayerPeer`
```gdscript
var peer = WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.new()
var result = peer.create_client("ws://localho2st:12345")
```
it produces `result == OK` and peer's state is `CONNECTION_CONNECTING`, but when using `ENetMultiplayerPeer`
```gdscript
var peer = ENetMultiplayerPeer.new()
var result = peer.create_client("localho2st", 12345)
```
it produces `result == ERR_CANT_CREATE`.

In documentation the only example uses `WebSocketPeer` instead of `WebSocketMultiplayerPeer` https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.4/tutorials/networking/websocket.html#minimal-client-example. But using `WebSocketPeer` produces the same result (`OK`) when using non-existing host info.

When checking the connection state using this simple code:
```gdscript
var t_start = Time.get_ticks_msec()
while true:
	peer.poll()
	if peer.get_connection_status() == WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.ConnectionStatus.CONNECTION_DISCONNECTED:
		print("timeout after: ", Time.get_ticks_msec() - t_start, "ms")
		break
	await get_tree().process_frame
```
The code prints `timeout after: 2287ms` (which I'm guessing is approximate timeout time).

Testing it in 4.5beta1 gives the same results.

This doesn't look like a bug. WSLPeer resolves hostnames asynchronously, while ENetMultiplayerPeer does so synchronously, so WebsocketMultiplayerPeer must be polled to check for this specific error. However, this is not documented at all, and there is no signal for this case (though adding one would be easy). It would also be nice to get error info from a failure, and WSLPeer exposes a close reason and close reason code (but does not populate in this case).

It also makes me wonder if ENetMultiplayerPeer _should_ be using the asynchonous hostname resolution, to make the behavior match up.
